title: Consumer commands are judged by the acting participant's `@mandate` profile; `ia position` stays ungated
summary: Breaking: @inventarch/cli now judges `ia read` and `ia next` (move Observation), `ia validate` and `ia preview` (Verification), `ia author` (Synthesis), and `ia capture`, its `ia compile` alias, `ia project` and a workspace `ia host <host> --apply`, which writes the same projection (Execution), by the acting participant's mandate profile (runtime governingMandates, defaultActor and profileRefusal) before they read or write anything; a capture or project plan is judged as the effect it plans, while a host plan, `ia host --remove` (which restores editing) and `ia host claude --user` are not judged. Where 2.0.0 ran these commands unconditionally, four cases now refuse them at exit 1: authored mandates that do not grant the mode's move, or, for preview and author only, exclude the word they write (IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-MOVE, -WORD); several authored participants and no authored `composition.steward`, an installed steward counting as none (IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR); a default actor, such as an authored steward the mandates do not name, that no governing mandate binds (IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR); and a governing mandate the runtime cannot read, such as `authority.moves []`, which admission accepts (IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID). A workspace `ia init` creates grants all five moves to its one participant, so its commands run as before, and a workspace with no governing mandate restricts nothing. `ia position` and every command outside those modes are not gated, so the governance position every refusal names always runs; neither are the Door's read, next and position operations (the MCP tools), the install, update and remove projection refresh, `ia-distribution validate`, `ia inspect` and the records route, `ia init`, and `ia host`'s plan, `--remove` and `--user`. Each gated command accepts --actor <agent> (a canonical identity, `@agent <name>` or a bare name), which must be an authored participant of the repository's `@workspace`: an authored `@agent` a mandate scoped to it names, or its `composition.steward` when that is an authored `@agent`; an installed steward is no default actor. Naming an actor is a local declaration, not authentication, accepted whether or not the workspace leaves the choice open: it resolves an open choice, or under a steward acts as another of the workspace's actors, and then that participant's own mandates are judged, which may be looser or stricter than the default actor's; it never lifts a move or excluded word those mandates state. Every refusal names one command that runs for the same actor in the same state: the governance position of the mandate concerned; under an open choice, or for a default actor no governing mandate binds, the same command with --actor naming the first participant whose mandates allow it (for an `ia author` form without a usable --digest, its `ia preview` form, which prints the digest); for an --actor that names no participant, the same command without it where the default actor may run it (for an `ia author` form without a usable --digest, again its `ia preview` form). Once a command's profile allows it, a refusal it raises later is held to the same rule: a next command of a gated mode the profile refuses becomes the governance position, and one it allows carries the named --actor. `ia project --apply` and a workspace `ia host --apply` write the rendering their gated plan session made, planned again against the files: a file changed since the plan still refuses, but a source or mandate change made while the confirmation question waits is not picked up, and `ia doctor` then reports the projection outdated. The machine routes, every `ia scope` form, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2 and the runtime's own refusals are unchanged. Limits: actor selection is not host authentication; a mandate restricts only the gated CLI commands, not the ungated surfaces above; the next-command rule holds for gated commands only, so an ungated command's refusal may name a gated command that then refuses with its own mandate refusal; the edit guard re-keyed to `@mandate` is separate work.
